title: Pod Stuck Pending — new node not scheduling
intro: You deployed a new batch-worker pod an hour ago and it's still not running.

steps.fake_output:
NAME                            READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
batch-worker-9f8d7c6b5-zx1qw   0/1     Pending   0          1h
steps.hint: Start with a basic status check.

steps.prompt: Find out why it's stuck Pending.
steps.fake_output:
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  1h  0/2 nodes are available: 2 node(s) had taint {dedicated: gpu}, that the pod didn't tolerate.
steps.hint: The Events section at the bottom of describe explains scheduling failures.

steps.prompt: Check the nodes and their taints.
expected_commands: kubectl describe node node-1 | grep Taints
steps.fake_output:
node-1   Ready   <none>   10d
node-2   Ready   <none>   10d

Taints: dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule
steps.hint: You want to see what taints exist on the available nodes.

steps.prompt: This pod doesn't need a GPU node. Since editing the taint isn't appropriate here (other pods rely on it), add a toleration to the pod's deployment instead — for this exercise, just confirm you'd edit the deployment.
steps.fake_output: (opens deployment.apps/batch-worker in your editor — add a tolerations block matching the taint, or remove the requirement so it can land on any untainted node)
steps.hint: In real life you'd add a tolerations entry to spec.template.spec.tolerations matching key=dedicated, value=gpu, effect=NoSchedule — but only if this workload genuinely belongs on GPU nodes. Otherwise the real fix is provisioning a non-tainted node.

resolution: All available nodes were tainted for GPU workloads, and this pod had no matching toleration, so the scheduler correctly refused to place it anywhere. Taints and tolerations exist precisely to reserve nodes for specific workloads — the fix is either giving the pod the right toleration (if it truly belongs there) or making sure non-GPU nodes exist for everything else.
